routes.description: Establish that multiple independent features of reality—including cosmic origins, life-permitting conditions, moral objectivity, the historical case concerning Jesus, and immediate experience—provide convergent support for a transcendent personal God.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if at least one major inference, or the cumulative interaction of several inferences, supplies a warranted bridge from the available evidence to supernatural personal agency while relevant naturalistic alternatives and epistemic objections are addressed.

motionBridge.description: Connect the cumulative philosophical, scientific, moral, historical, and experiential evidence to the conclusion that God's existence is supported.

centralBridges.description: Show that the universe's beginning or life-permitting structure warrants an inference to transcendent personal causation or design.
Show that objective moral values and duties are real and require a foundation beyond naturalistic processes or collective human practice.
Show that the historical claims concerning Jesus are sufficiently grounded and are best accounted for by divine action.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify the deductive, explanatory, or cumulative form of the theistic inferences and the burden applicable to their premises.
Establish when immediate moral or religious experience may provide warranted belief absent a sufficient defeater.

routes.description: Establish philosophical naturalism as the warranted position by affirming the known natural world and showing that the proposed cosmological, design, moral, historical, and experiential bridges to supernatural reality lack sufficient justification.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the available evidence does not warrant any proposed bridge from nature to God and continued natural explanation or withholding supernatural belief remains justified without requiring proof that every supernatural possibility is impossible.

motionBridge.description: Show that the available evidence does not provide a sufficiently justified bridge from known nature to God's existence.

centralBridges.description: Defend evidential restraint toward untestable supernatural claims while explaining why belief in known nature may be retained.
Preserve live natural explanations or relevant uncertainty for cosmic origins and life-permitting conditions.
Explain how objective but nonabsolute morality can arise through human experience, comparison, deliberation, and social practice.
Show that historical testimony, miracle reports, and conflicting religious experiences do not uniquely establish supernatural causation.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Clarify why withholding supernatural belief can be compatible with either atheistic or agnostic terminology.
Determine whether adaptable theological explanations discriminate among favorable, unfavorable, and religiously conflicting observations.

sections.title: Epistemic Burdens, Inference Form, and Naturalism
sections.rationale: This issue governs what counts as an evidential bridge beyond nature, whether theistic arguments are deductive or explanatory, and whether failed supernatural inferences warrant naturalism, atheism, agnosticism, or suspended judgment.

sections.title: Cosmic Beginning and Transcendent Causation
sections.rationale: The universe's temporal or causal origin supplies a direct proposed route beyond physical reality, while questions about infinity, timeless personhood, and further natural reality test whether that route reaches God.

sections.title: Fine-Tuning, Alternative Life, and Design
sections.rationale: The evidential significance of life-permitting constants depends on necessity, chance, probability spaces, possible forms of life, broader cosmic populations, and whether design provides a discriminating explanation.

sections.title: Objective Morality, Knowledge, and Grounding
sections.rationale: Moral experience and objective obligation form a principal proposed inference to God, while distinctions among ontology, knowledge, absoluteness, intersubjective practice, evolution, and moral progress define the central clash.

sections.title: Resurrection, Historical Sources, and Miracle Claims
sections.rationale: The specifically Christian route turns on the historical use of New Testament materials, corroboration standards, natural alternatives, testimony, and whether resurrection or miracle claims warrant an inference to divine action.

sections.title: Religious Experience and Conflicting Revelations
sections.rationale: Immediate experience is offered as direct warrant for God, while incompatible religious reports and the need for a method of corroboration bear on whether such experience identifies supernatural truth.
